extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, newsroom leadership, journalism educators
extracted.subtask_description: A case-focused analysis of a high-profile journalistic failure (Rolling Stone's 'A Rape on Campus') identifying lapses in reporting, editing, and fact-checking and recommending changes to newsroom practices. The report reviews source handling, corroboration, editorial oversight, and the responsibilities of a news organization when errors occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine asked an outside team to investigate 'any lapses in reporting, editing and fact-checking behind the story.' The report treats reporting failures as central to the case and examines how the reporter gathered and presented the story, including reliance on a single principal source and narrative choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing is named explicitly (paired with reporting and fact-checking) as an area where the magazine may have failed; the report looks at editorial oversight, how editors handled source material and the story's narrative, and whether edits contributed to unverified or problematic presentation of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Columbia team was asked to examine failures in fact-checking. The narrative cites the Washington Post uncovering details that suggested 'the assault could not have taken place the way we described it,' implying the need for rigorous verification of timelines, physical plausibility, and corroborating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent outside review
rubrics_metrics.description: Use independent, external investigation to assess failures and recommend reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rolling Stone 'decided the only responsible and credible thing to do was to ask someone from outside the magazine to investigate' and agreed the team would 'receive no payment' and that the magazine would 'cooperate fully' and publish the report in full—guidance on how to conduct credible post‑mortem reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability: retraction and apology
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting is shown to be wrong, publicly retract and apologize to affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the report's publication, Rolling Stone states 'we are officially retracting 'A Rape on Campus.'' The editor apologizes to readers and to those harmed by the story and fallout, signaling newsroom responsibilities after errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to recommendations and practice change
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt and implement recommendations about journalistic practices arising from the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor states the magazine is 'committing ourselves to a series of recommendations about journalistic practices that are spelled out in the report,' indicating that post‑error remedies should be concrete, public, and implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source vetting and credibility assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly vet sources and evaluate credibility beyond initial referrals or apparent authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporter felt the student 'had this stamp of credibility' because a university employee connected them, and previous testimony had referenced the allegations. The report implies that such perceived credibility from referrals is insufficient without independent corroboration and deeper vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration of anonymous or protected sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely solely on a single anonymous source for major factual claims; seek independent corroboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story centered on a single principal source ('Jackie' a pseudonym). The report examines how reliance on one account—especially an anonymized one—without robust corroboration contributed to the failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward narrative-driven selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid shaping reporting to fit an intended emblematic narrative; ensure evidence supports the chosen frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor notes Rolling Stone was 'searching for a single, emblematic college rape case' to illustrate a broader issue. The report treats the risk of selecting or molding a case to fit a narrative as a contributing factor to errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of physical and temporal details
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm timelines and physical feasibility of events described in a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Washington Post 'uncovered details suggesting that the assault could not have taken place the way we described it,' highlighting the need to verify time stamps, locations, and whether described actions were possible given known facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to memory limitations and testimonial uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that witnesses' memories may be imperfect and treat memory gaps as a reason to seek corroboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A source told the reporter 'maybe her memory of it isn’t perfect,' and the writer's notes record a readiness to accept the account as 'totally plausible.' The report underscores that plausibility is not a substitute for verification when memory is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about investigative methods and publication of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about how an internal or external investigation was conducted and publish findings publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rolling Stone promised the Columbia team could 'take as much time as they needed and write whatever they wanted' and that the magazine would 'publish their report in full,' modeling transparency in addressing newsroom failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest in corrective investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure independence (e.g., no payment) to avoid perceived conflicts in post‑error inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes the external investigators 'would receive no payment,' a procedural detail meant to protect the independence and credibility of the review.
